predictions.prediction_text: The market expects either a move up above 6900 or a move down to retest past weeks' lows to build a base.
predictions.expected_result: Either an upside breakout above 6900 or a downside retest of recent lows forming a consolidation/base will occur.

predictions.prediction_text: Weak GDP data will lead the market to price in more Fed easing and be supportive of risk assets.
predictions.expected_result: Markets will rally or stabilize as Fed easing expectations increase.

predictions.prediction_text: Strong GDP data will erase concerns about future easing and reduce liquidity support, leading to a less supportive market reaction.
predictions.expected_result: Markets will fall or lose upward momentum as Fed easing odds are reduced.

predictions.prediction_text: A positive supply-side GDP print (GDP up, prices down) will produce a risk-on market reaction.
A negative demand-side GDP print (GDP down, prices down) will be benign overall but produce an initially pessimistic market reaction.
predictions.expected_result: Immediate market weakness followed by stabilization or muted gains.

predictions.prediction_text: A positive demand-side GDP print (GDP up, prices up) will trigger an initial pessimistic re-pricing of Fed cut odds.
predictions.expected_result: Initial market decline as Fed cut expectations are repriced lower.

predictions.prediction_text: A negative supply-side GDP print (GDP down, prices up) will be stagflationary and cause a clearly negative market reaction.
The most likely outcome is modestly-above-consensus GDP with inflation in-line to slightly softer, which will produce a slow or delayed positive market digestion.
predictions.expected_result: Markets will take time to move higher or stabilize as the data is digested under a 'data not fully collected' narrative.
